unit: Fixed-measure psh continuity and canonical grid self-integral convergence
files_read: Complete new chapters/inputs/q08-grid-energy-convergence.tex directly read twice around the first build and visual inspection; changed history paragraphs and input seams checked. Final Needspace-only seam adjustment directly read. Scoped unit reads only.
Exact earlier Q02 local Lp/Hartogs, Q08 zero-capacity envelope discrepancy and the verified energy-moment/grid interfaces consulted; prior verification evidence retained.
source_locators_checked: Exact Dinew0705.0974v1 Theorem2.2 statement pp.4–5 and its quoted self-integral attribution directly read, with both original images inspected. Bibliography Ce1/Ce2 metadata on p.12 consulted only. Theorem2.3 capacity statement is context, not adopted; Cegrell1998 proofs are not claimed read. Source n-fold measure normalization remains (4pi)^n times ours.
proof_scope: Bounded fixed-measure continuity for finite measures ignoring local zero outer capacity; canonical tail envelopes and Borel discrepancy; minimum-norm finite convex tail combinations, parallelogram/Cauchy and direct L2 completeness; subsequence integral separation and Hartogs positive part; uniform second moments/truncation; finite-center shifted-psh cell averages; convergence in finite measure plus Cauchy–Schwarz; signed and positive parts give moving-measure absolute convergence. Zero measure, dimension one, unbounded canonical limit and its null pole set explicit. No later Hilbert theorem, capacity stability, limit equation or unbounded product imported.
review_method: Two scoped direct mathematical/editorial reads by the authoring agent, not independent certification. Fourteen first selected pages inspected. After a final display-seam adjustment all449 pages rendered against the first build again, and all five final changes directly inspected. Pixel-identical first pages retain visual review.
remaining_obligations: Canonical capacity and limit-equation closure; bounded-subsolution solvability.
General common-measure mixed inequality, unweighted relative uniqueness and earlier FN/positivity/envelope PDE/overlap/whole-prequel polishing gates.
